subject: doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/autopilot-full.md
why: New playbook, owner rulings of 2026-11-20 (2026-11-20-deferred-playbooks:005) and 2026-11-23 (answers on the adaptation proposal), decision cr-0qcj, and the coordinator's fix-round rulings of 2026-11-23. Steps: (1) intake of settled beads only, an open question labelled human and skipped, independence stated with evidence and the concurrency set by the owner's go (one at a time by default, lowered mid-run after the current task), and the run marker taken last through autopilot-full/run_marker.py, created exclusively with the run's id, refusing to start while one exists; (2) a branch per feature from fresh trunk in its own worktree, never stacked, a worker per feature through delegation when parallel, shared state per principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state, the first push with upstream tracking and a push after each finished task with a bead resume line; (3) each bead built with implement's Task loop run as this playbook's own step (not the implement playbook called whole), task beads closed with evidence and the feature's bead left open until its merge, implement's per-unit review left out because the feature's one review replaces it; (4) the commit gate at every commit point (a build commit, a trunk merge, babysit's publish): autopilot-full/commit_gate.py runs the project's .repo-context/commit-gate.toml as the commit holds it, staged checks then project checks, cheapest first, refusing a tree or a gate file that differs from the commit, a skipped optional tool shown as SKIP, manual checks done from the verification guide before the commit and noted on the bead with the new commit's SHA, a missing gate file drafted for the owner's approval; (5) a friction pattern stops the feature for the owner; (6) code-ready: trunk merged in (never a rebase of a pushed branch), the staged merge gated, its manual checks done, then committed as one two-parent commit (git commit --no-edit, not land) and noted with its SHA, the gate with --since on the merged tip printing the range it judged and its manual checks done on that range and noted with the tip SHA, nothing to ship when trunk already holds the feature, push, open the pull request through pr, which creates and mirrors no issue here (Closes only the bead's own issue, no line when the chain has none); (7) one independent review on the pull request, recorded as Shipping records a verdict, a verdict for every later head's tree (a re-check confirming prose only for a wording change), babysit in drive mode within the grant (no reruns, no mirroring, no closeout writes), merge-ready only with a usable verdict for the current tree; (8) only a shown problem blocks, the rest become follow-ups; (9) a held write, a foreign push or a rejected push stops that feature, checked before every push; (10) the owner's stop means no further writes; (11) closeout keeps worktrees while pull requests are open, cleanup after a merge through worktree-cleanup, discards held, claims released, the marker released last only while it holds this run's id. Gates: the delivery grant, the held writes (AGENTS.md Authority plus merging, closing an epic, history rewrites, forge writes outside the grant and gate loosening), no force-push at all, called units bound to the grant, and the branch guard hook the marker turns on (Bash writes not covered).

subject: ours:mvp-mode

The catalog is unchanged (no new skill). Tree hash refreshed.

subject: cursor_plugins:skill:pstack/skills/architect#scrap-on-repeated-friction
why: Delivered by cr-p3em.4 (owner ruling 2026-11-22, rejections re-review, bead cr-r2pa.3.3): a pattern that shows a feature's sketch is wrong (the same workaround recurring, special-case branches piling up, type escapes, repeated deviations), not one isolated problem, stops that feature: noted on the bead, labelled human, its committed work pushed, and the run moves to the next feature (.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/autopilot-full.md:152-156). The playbook lists the trait on autopilot-full#5.

subject: mattpocock_skills:skill:skills/misc/setup-pre-commit#commit-time-checks
why: Delivered by cr-p3em.4 (owner rulings 2026-11-22 and 2026-11-23, answer 2: hybrid gate, script first): every commit a run makes, a worker's included, at every commit point (a build commit, a trunk merge, babysit's publish), first passes the commit gate, a standard-library script beside the playbook (autopilot-full/commit_gate.py) that runs the project's own checks from .repo-context/commit-gate.toml on the staged paths; a failure stops the commit, fixed and rerun, never skipped, and the manual checks it prints are done before the commit and noted with the new commit's SHA once it succeeds (.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/autopilot-full.md:132-151). A build or babysit commit then goes through land; a trunk merge commits directly, as step 6 says. It is not a git hook, because this repository's hooks path belongs to Beads, which :035 left to this build to design around; the agent runs it before each commit. Which checks run (formatting, lint, types, tests) is the project's gate file, here every scriptable row of .repo-context/verification.md. The playbook lists the trait on autopilot-full#4.

subject: mattpocock_skills:skill:skills/misc/setup-pre-commit#cheap-checks-first

subject: superpowers:skill:skills/finishing-a-development-branch#checks-on-integrated-tree
why: Delivered by cr-p3em.4: trunk is merged into a feature's branch, the staged merge is gated (never refused as empty), its manual checks done before the commit, then committed as one commit of the whole index (git commit --no-edit, not land) with both parents checked and the results noted with the merge commit's SHA; then the commit gate runs with --since on the committed tip with a clean tree and prints the exact range it judged, each manual check it prints is done on that range and noted on the bead with the range and the tip's SHA, every check given the judged range reads the range it prints, and nothing is pushed for the pull request until both pass, a failure fixed by a new gated commit and a tip with nothing changed since trunk stopped as nothing to ship (.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/autopilot-full.md:157-176). The gate judges that tip: it reads the gate file from HEAD by its repository-relative name and refuses a working copy that differs or is not a regular file, its whitespace check reads the merge-base..HEAD range, and the trunk merge's own commit is gated even when it brings no change (autopilot-full/commit_gate.py; regressions in tests/checks/test_commit_gate.py). The project's gate file names the checks, in place of one fixed test command. The playbook lists the trait on autopilot-full#6.

subject: superpowers:skill:skills/finishing-a-development-branch#push-and-open-pr
why: Delivered by cr-p3em.4: the branch's first push sets upstream tracking (git push -u origin <branch>, .claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/autopilot-full.md:104-114), and once the merged tip passes the gate the branch is pushed and its pull request opened against trunk with gh pr create, its body through pr, Closes only for the bead's own issue when the pull request completes it (.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/autopilot-full.md:157-176), under the owner's grant; the reply names each pull request by its full address. The playbook lists the trait on autopilot-full#6.

subject: superpowers:skill:skills/finishing-a-development-branch#keep-worktree-until-landed
why: Delivered by cr-p3em.4: the closeout keeps each feature's worktree and branch while its pull request is open, because review fixes land there, and after a merge cleanup goes through the worktree-cleanup playbook (.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/autopilot-full.md:211-218). The playbook lists the trait on autopilot-full#11.

subject: superpowers:skill:skills/finishing-a-development-branch#rejected-push-investigation
why: Delivered by cr-p3em.4: a rejected push stops the feature, and the run finds out why (the remote moved, a hook or a rule refused) and reports it, never forcing (.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/autopilot-full.md:200-206); the run makes no force-push, and any rewrite of pushed history is a held write made only when the owner explicitly asks (.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/autopilot-full.md:78-80). The playbook lists the trait on autopilot-full#9.

why: Owner rulings 2026-11-22 and 2026-11-23 (answer 4), bead cr-p3em.4: Autopilot-full makes no merge, and after the owner merges, cleanup goes through worktree-cleanup, which keeps branch refs and treats deleting one as a separate request.

subject: superpowers:skill:skills/finishing-a-development-branch#typed-discard-confirmation
why: Owner rulings 2026-11-22 and 2026-11-23 (answer 4), bead cr-p3em.4: Autopilot-full never discards; discarding unmerged work is held for the owner under AGENTS.md's rule to show what would be lost and get explicit confirmation, and a fixed typed word adds nothing to the owner's own message.

subject: superpowers:skill:skills/finishing-a-development-branch#provenance-worktree-cleanup
why: Owner rulings 2026-11-22 and 2026-11-23 (answer 4), bead cr-p3em.4: cleanup after a merge goes through worktree-cleanup, which removes only the worktrees the owner approves by exact path and never prunes globally; a location convention would decide removal without that approval.

subject: The-Claude-Protocol:hook:templates/hooks/enforce-branch-before-edit
why: Owner rulings 2026-11-22 (rejections re-review, bead cr-r2pa.3.3: adopt the hook that refuses edits on the default branch) and 2026-11-23 (answer 3: only while an Autopilot run is active), superseding the defer 2026-11-22-rejects-review:057 ("until built"). Our hook refuses Edit, Write, MultiEdit and NotebookEdit only while the run marker exists in the repository's common git dir and the checkout the edited file lands in is on the default branch; every other edit passes, so ordinary sessions are unaffected. A hook keeps one ruling per capability with no trait analysis (README §4a), so its parts and the rulings on each are in `adaptation`.

merged_from: reference_harnesses/The-Claude-Protocol/templates/hooks/enforce-branch-before-edit.sh:9-16, 36-50 (a PreToolUse hook on Edit and Write that refuses the edit when the current branch is main or master)
modifications: Active only during an Autopilot-full run: it refuses only while the marker `autopilot-run` exists in the common git dir (git rev-parse --git-common-dir), which every worktree of the repository shares; the playbook takes it at intake through autopilot-full/run_marker.py, an exclusive create holding the run's id, and releases it at exit only while it holds that id, so a second run cannot take or clear the first run's marker (owner answer 3).
The payload is read with a JSON decoder, jq or else Python's json module; with neither, every edit is refused while the session's repository holds a marker.
The branch is read from the checkout holding the edited file (its nearest existing folder for a new file), not from the session's working directory, and a detached HEAD passes.
The default branch is origin/HEAD's target; without it, main and master.
Covers MultiEdit and NotebookEdit beside Edit and Write.
The refusal is exit 2 with the reason on stderr, like our other guards, and names the marker path so a marker a crash left behind can be cleared.
deliberately_dropped: Always on (enforce-branch-before-edit.sh:3-6): owner answer 3 keeps ordinary sessions unaffected.
The .worktrees/ path and working-directory exemptions (enforce-branch-before-edit.sh:23-34): judging the edited file's own checkout makes a worktree on a feature branch pass with no path convention.
The plan-file exemption (enforce-branch-before-edit.sh:18-21): a file outside any repository passes anyway.
The worktree-API instructions in the refusal text (enforce-branch-before-edit.sh:41-47): specific to that harness's server.
Shell-made writes stay uncovered, as upstream: a limit the playbook states.

subject: cursor_plugins:playbook:pstack/skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/autopilot-full
why: Map 2.18 and the owner rulings of 2026-11-20 (ride on Beads and the implement playbook; grant: commit, push a working branch and open a pull request without asking; merging, closing an epic, other network writes and repository settings need the owner's word) and 2026-11-23 (the four answers on the adaptation proposal), with decision cr-0qcj (one pull request per feature, its one review there). Supersedes the defer 2026-11-20-deferred-playbooks:005.

modifications: Rides on Beads and the implement playbook: intake takes only settled beads, an open question is labelled human and skipped, and each bead is built with implement's Task loop run as this playbook's own step, without implement's per-unit review, with delegation choosing workers; the feature's one review replaces the per-unit review.

Concurrency is the owner's per-run choice (answer 1): intake states independence with evidence and proposes; the owner's go sets it, one at a time by default, lowered mid-run after the current task; parallel features each get a worktree off fresh trunk and a worker, shared state per principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state.

A commit gate at every commit point (answer 2): a script beside the playbook runs the project's gate file as the commit holds it, staged checks then project checks, cheapest first, refusing a tree or gate file that differs from the commit; manual checks from the verification guide, noted on the bead.
A branch guard hook during a run only (answer 3), switched on by a marker in the common git dir that the run creates exclusively and releases only while it holds the run's id.

One review per feature at its code-ready head on its pull request (cr-0qcj), from another model family through delegation, recorded as Shipping records a verdict so Shipping can reuse it; every later head's tree gets a verdict sized by the change as upstream, a wording-only change a re-check confirming prose only, and merge-ready needs a usable verdict for the current tree.

Owner holds: AGENTS.md's standing-grant list, plus merging, closing an epic, history rewrites, forge writes outside the grant and gate loosening; no force-push at all, trunk brought in by a merge; pr and babysit run bound to the grant (no issue created or mirrored, no workflow rerun, no closeout write); a foreign or rejected push stops that feature.
A friction pattern stops the feature for the owner (scrap-on-repeated-friction); finishing pushes and opens the pull request, cleanup after a merge through worktree-cleanup, discards held (answer 4).
deliberately_dropped: Cloud-agent owners, one per pull request: delegation picks workers. revisit_when: never for the vendor.
The owner merges and the merge-time rebase rules (step 5): merging is held for the owner and Shipping owns the trunk check and the merge. revisit_when: the owner grants merging.
The root countersigns gate loosening (step 6): there is no root above the owner; loosening is held for the owner.

The hourly loop audit of stuck agents and the catch-up skill: delegates run in the foreground and are judged by their commits; the reply contract replaces the catch-up. revisit_when: background delegates enter our toolchain.
Origin forge, Graphite, the slop and comment passes and the control skills: gh only, unslop for prose, the project's own way of running the change.
The decision trail in the root's store: the bead's resume line and notes carry the trail.
